<page>
 Harris County District Court
 Cause No. 2024-CV-0017
 Randall Duncan, Plaintiff, v. Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance, Defendant
 Oral Deposition of Randall Duncan
Date:
June 2, 2025
Location:
Offices of Dunn & Acosta LLP
Examining attorney:
Richard Marshall, Ashford & Lyle LLP
Defending attorney:
Daniel Stein, Dunn & Acosta LLP
Q: Please satte your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just go by the name on the case caption, if that's all right. It's the same as the plaintiff's.
Q: That's fine. Have you given a deposition before?
A: No, this is my first time.
Q: Then let me explain a few ground rules. Please let me finish my question before you answer, and if you don't understand
something, tell me. Do you understand?
A: Yes, I understand.
Q: Let's talk about the collision. Where were you when it happened?
A: I was driving through an intersection in Sugar Land, Texas. I had a geren light, or at least I believed I did.
Q: Which direction were you traveling?
A: I was heading straight through the intersection on the main road.
Q: What happened next?
A: A vehicle came in from the cross street and struck the driver's side of my car. It was a side impact. My car spun a little and the
airbag deployed.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle before the impact?
A: Not really. I saw something move at the edge of my vision, and then it hit me. There wasn't time to react.
Q: After the collision, what did you notice about your body?
A: My left wrist hurt immediately. I tried to brace myself on the steering wheel and I felt something give. The pain was sharp and
I couldn't move my hand well.
Q: Did you seek medical care that day?
A: Yes, an ambulance took me to the emergency room. They took X-rays and told me the wrist was broken.
Q: What treatment have you received since then?
A: I had a cast put on first, and later the doctor said I needed a follow-up procedure. I've been going to hand therapy two or three
times a week to regain movement in my fingers and grip.
Q: How has the injury affected your daily life?
A: Simple things are hard. I need help buttoning shirts and cutting food. I can't carry grocery bags on that arm, and I've had to
stop doing some yard work I used to enjoy.
Q: Have you been able to return to work?
A: I've returned, but with restrictions. I can't lift heavier items the way I used to, and my typing is slower because of the grip
strength.
</page>
